expected_answer: The 4% development levy applies to the assessable profits of companies other than small companies and non-resident companies, so a small company does not pay it (NTA Section 59(1)).
must_not: states that a small company pays the development levy

expected_answer: Where a Nigerian company declares a dividend out of profits on which no tax is payable because it has no total profits, it is charged to tax at the Section 56 rate as if the dividend were its total profits for the year (NTA Section 9(1)).
This does not apply to dividends out of retained earnings already taxed, out of exempt profits, franked investment income, or certain real estate investment company distributions (NTA Section 9(2)).
must_not: states that the dividend goes untaxed because the company made no profit
rationale: Section 9(1) answers; 9(2) gives the exceptions a reader needs.

expected_answer: No deduction is allowed for a penalty or fine imposed under any law (NTA Section 21(l)).
must_not: states that fines paid to a regulator are deductible

expected_answer: Gains of an individual on disposing of a dwelling-house, and adjoining non-commercial land up to one acre, are exempt (NTA Section 51(1)).
The exemption can be used only once in an individual's lifetime (NTA Section 51(2)).
must_not: states that the gain on the home is always taxable

expected_answer: Where input VAT exceeds output VAT, the taxable person may use the excess as a credit against later months (NTA Section 156(1)(b)).
Excess VAT not used as a credit may be refunded on request to the Service, with the information it requires (NTA Section 156(2)).
must_not: states that the excess is lost or must be paid to the Service
rationale: Section 156(1)(b) answers the question; 156(2) is the refund route a reader needs next.

expected_answer: Where a non-resident makes taxable supplies from outside Nigeria to persons in Nigeria, the Nigerian taxable person receiving the supply must withhold the VAT and remit it to the Service (NTA Section 151(2)).
If the Service has appointed the supplier to collect the VAT, the Nigerian recipient need not withhold it unless the appointed person failed to collect it (NTA Section 151(3)-(4)).
must_not: states that no VAT is due because the supplier is outside Nigeria

expected_answer: Basic food items are charged to VAT at 0% (NTA Section 187(a)).
Basic food items include cereals such as rice, and flours including cassava flakes (garri) (NTA Section 189, "basic food items" (c), (g)).
must_not: states that VAT at 7.5% applies to the rice and garri
states that the items are exempt supplies rather than zero-rated
rationale: Section 187(a) zero-rates basic food items; the definition brings rice and garri in. Item (m) also covers cassava flakes.

expected_answer: Baby products are exempt from VAT (NTA Section 186(1)(d)).
Baby products include sanitary wares such as diapers, for babies from birth to three years (NTA Section 189, "baby products" (g)).
must_not: states that VAT at 7.5% is charged on diapers
rationale: Section 186(1)(d) exempts baby products; the definition lists diapers.

expected_answer: A small company has turnover of ₦50,000,000 or less and fixed assets not exceeding ₦250,000,000, but a business providing professional services is not a small company (NTA Section 202, "small company").
Professional services include consulting (NTA Section 202, "professional services").
must_not: states that a low-turnover consulting firm qualifies as a small company

expected_answer: A company is connected to another where the same person controls both, or connected persons acting separately control them (NTA Section 202, "connected persons" (d)(ii)).

Two companies are connected where one participates directly or indirectly in the management, control or capital of the other, or the same persons participate in both (NTA Section 202, "connected persons" (d)(iv)).
must_not: states that two companies are connected only because one is a client of the other
rationale: Paragraph (d) of the definition answers; the participation definition sets the 30% control test.

expected_answer: Motor vehicle expenditure is in Class 3, with an annual capital allowance rate of 25% (NTA First Schedule, Table I).
must_not: states a rate other than 25%

expected_answer: Interest paid to a connected person in excess of 30% of the company's earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation for the period is not deductible (NTA Third Schedule, paragraphs 1-2).
Excess interest not deducted can be carried forward for up to five assessment years (NTA Third Schedule, paragraph 4).
must_not: states that interest paid to a sister company is deductible without limit
rationale: The Third Schedule answers; Section 20(1)(a) makes interest deductible subject to it.

expected_answer: A company in business for more than 18 months files not more than six months after the end of its accounting year (NTAA Section 11(5)(a)).
must_not: gives the newly incorporated company's 18-month rule as this company's deadline
rationale: The question says the company has traded for several years, so paragraph (a) applies.

expected_answer: A small company's return may contain a statement of accounts attested by the taxpayer instead of audited financial statements (NTAA Section 11(1)(b), proviso).
must_not: states that a small company must always attach audited financial statements

expected_answer: The relevant tax authority may raise an additional assessment within six years of the assessment (NTAA Section 36(1)).
A tax audit begun before the six years end may continue and lead to an additional assessment (NTAA Section 36(2)).
Where there is a deliberate misstatement, the authority may assess at any time (NTAA Section 36(4)).
must_not: states a limitation period other than six years

expected_answer: Where a business shows no assessable profit or less than expected, or its profit cannot readily be ascertained, the relevant tax authority may assess a resident on a fair and reasonable percentage of the gross income of the trade (NTAA Section 38(1)(a)).
must_not: states that the tax office must accept records showing almost no profit

expected_answer: Collection of tax under objection or appeal is held in abeyance until the objection or appeal is decided (NTAA Section 49(3)).
The taxpayer must still pay the tax that is not the subject of the objection or appeal (NTAA Section 49(3)).
must_not: states that the full disputed amount must be paid while the objection is pending

expected_answer: On a valid request, the Service must refund the VAT, or allow it to be set off against other tax liability, not later than 30 days after receiving the request (NTAA Section 56(3)).
The request must be made within 12 months of the transaction giving rise to the refund, or it lapses (NTAA Section 56(2)).
must_not: gives the 90-day general refund period as the VAT refund deadline

expected_answer: A company in an arrangement with a related party must ensure its terms are at arm's length and report the arrangement as the relevant tax authority prescribes (NTA Section 192(1)).
Where an arrangement is not at arm's length, the relevant tax authority may adjust it to arm's length terms under the Transfer Pricing Regulations (NTA Section 192(2)).
must_not: describes section 192 as being about a subject other than related-party arrangements at arm's length
rationale: A summary of Section 192's main rules.

expected_answer: The relevant tax authority may, for good cause shown, remit all or part of a penalty or interest due under the Act or any other tax law (NTAA Section 66).
It must make a monthly report to the Minister or commissioner for finance with details of the taxpayers, circumstances and amounts waived (NTAA Section 66).
must_not: states that penalties or interest can never be waived
rationale: Section 66 is one sentence; both parts summarised.
